newsitem.title: USA: Snow-choked Midwest digs out; new cold on way.
newsitem.headline: Snow-choked Midwest digs out; new cold on way.

text.p: Sunny skies and the promise of a brief warm-up spurred dig-out efforts across the snow-choked upper Midwest on Tuesday, and forecasters said more cold weather was on the way in the eastern United States.
Winter's grip was deadly from the Midwest to traditionally warmer states in the South and by Tuesday more than 30 people were estimated to have died across the country.
Much of the United States from the Rockies eastward has been iced by temperatures well below or near zero Fahrenheit (minus 18 Celsius) since late last week.
Texas officials said the storm was responsible for 11 deaths in the state in traffic accidents on icy roads.
"We have reports of eleven dead. That's from reports of accidents investigated by (state police)," said Sherri Deatherage Green, spokeswoman with the Texas Department of Public Safety.
The ice storm also closed roads and schools and blacked out homes and businesses across much of the state.
One of the most tragic incidents reported in the country was in Austin, Minn. where a paraplegic who fell from his wheel chair was found frozen to death at his home.

Homeless shelters were at capacity in the Minneapolis-St. Paul area. Gov. Arne Carlson asked for federal disaster aid for western and southwestern parts of the state where cities and counties have exhausted their snow-fighting budgets.
In Milwaukee, churches were asked to take in homeless people who could not find room in shelters.

Snowbound livestock were dying across North Dakota. At the town of Selfridge, workers cut a new road into town across a pasture after eight foot (2.5 metre) drifts blocked normal routes. Residents were reported running out of food and fuel.
Wayne Carlson, livestock director for North Dakota, said a state task force was working to estimate how many cattle had died as a result of the severe winter weather.
"I've heard estimates that 10,000 animals across the state are in dire need of feed or haven't been fed in a while," Carlson said.
In upstate New York, arctic winds blowing across Lake Ontario left hip-high snow falls. Nearly eight feet (2.5 metres) of snow was reported at Montague, N.Y.
Heavy snow fell across parts of Colorado, improving an already booming ski season, and ski resorts in mountain areas of the southeast were making snow with the help of the frigid temperatures.

Forecasters said some temporary relief was on the way with a warmup of as much as 20 degrees from Colorado westward. However, they warned that cold weather would return to the east by the end of the week.
